boards.school_name: The University of Texas at Arlington
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UTA traditions, from mud volleyball and wheeled beds to ceremonial rings and campus art horses.

cards.title: Oozeball Tournament
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Join or watch teams play mud volleyball in ankle-deep muck during this fall Campus Recreation event; proceeds benefit student scholarships.
cards.short_summary: UTA’s muddy volleyball tradition has been held each fall since 1989.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA identifies Oozeball as a fall mud-volleyball tournament held since 1989 and says its proceeds benefit student scholarships.
cards.access_notes: Check the official UTA traditions page or events calendar for the current fall event details.

cards.title: MavsMeet Convocation
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Start the fall term at UTA’s new-Maverick welcome in Texas Hall, then look for the accompanying AfterParty with music, games, and food.
cards.short_summary: An academic-year kickoff that formally welcomes new Mavericks.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA describes MavsMeet Convocation as a tradition that welcomes new Mavericks and officially begins the academic year before fall classes.
cards.access_notes: UTA says the convocation is held in Texas Hall the day before fall classes; verify the current schedule before attending.

cards.title: Bed Races
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Watch themed teams push wheeled beds across stadium turf, or follow Student Activities announcements for participation and current event details.
cards.short_summary: UTA teams race wheeled beds in a tradition begun for Maverick Stadium’s opening.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA says Bed Races began in 1980 to celebrate Maverick Stadium’s opening and continue as an annual competition.
cards.access_notes: The official Student Activities page says Bed Races continue annually as part of Spirit Week; confirm the current date and participation rules.

cards.title: UTA Homecoming
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Follow the November Homecoming schedule for the campus celebration, including the Blue & White events, coronation, and Maverick Step Show.
cards.short_summary: A November welcome-back celebration tied to UTA basketball and Maverick spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA states that Homecoming is held in November to welcome alumni and celebrate its men’s and women’s basketball teams.
cards.access_notes: Event components vary by year; use UTA’s official Homecoming information when the current program is announced.

cards.title: Maverick Stampede
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Use the start-of-year event lineup to meet people, explore campus opportunities, and get oriented to UTA life before settling into the semester.
cards.short_summary: UTA’s official new-academic-year kickoff is built around a series of campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA identifies Maverick Stampede as the official kickoff to a new academic year, with events for fun, connection, and acclimation.
cards.access_notes: Consult UTA’s official Stampede schedule for the current year’s activities, locations, and attendance details.

cards.title: Grad Cap Contest
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: If graduating, photograph a decorated cap and submit it through the official contest process during the semester’s Commencement activities.
cards.short_summary: Graduation candidates share decorated-cap photos in a recurring UTA contest.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA says graduation candidates submit photos of decorated caps for prizes in a contest held during Commencement events each semester.
cards.access_notes: Eligibility and submission instructions are announced with each semester’s Commencement programming.

cards.title: The University Mace
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Spot this ceremonial staff during academic processions and read its maker story before Commencement or another formal University ceremony.
cards.short_summary: UTA’s ceremonial mace was created in 2007 by artists David Keens and Fred Miller.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA states that its University Mace was designed and created in 2007 by Texas State Artist and professor David Keens with adjunct professor Fred Miller.
cards.access_notes: The mace is part of formal academic processions; observe it during public ceremonial events when present.

cards.title: Official Maverick Ring Ceremony
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Eligible ring purchasers can watch for the twice-yearly ceremony before finals, where recipients receive rings alongside University leaders.
cards.short_summary: A twice-yearly ceremonial presentation for purchasers of the Official Maverick Ring.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA says the Official Maverick Ring Ceremony is held twice yearly before finals for students who purchase the official ring.
cards.access_notes: UTA specifies that recipients purchase an Official Maverick Ring; check Alumni Relations for eligibility and ceremony registration.

cards.title: International Week
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Plan for the parade of banners, cultural displays, food fair, fashion show, and Global Extravaganza during UTA’s annual international celebration.
cards.short_summary: A weeklong UTA celebration of its international student community, running since 1977.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA says International Week has celebrated the cultures of its international student population since 1977 through a weeklong program.
cards.access_notes: Programs and participation details change by year; consult UTA’s official event listings for the current International Week schedule.

cards.title: Spirit Horse Program
cards.subtitle: UTA tradition • Arlington, Texas
cards.notes: Look for the decorated fiberglass horses around campus and use the official program information to understand the community art project behind them.
cards.short_summary: Decorated fiberglass horses continue a UTA community public-art tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA says its Spirit Horses began as a community public-art project and remain an ongoing tradition of decorated horses around campus.
cards.access_notes: Horses are campus art objects; view them only from publicly accessible areas and do not climb or alter them.
